content.tldr: Time travel allows analytic engines to query historical states of a table using a past timestamp or snapshot ID, enabling auditability, regression debugging, and rollback.
content.simple_explanation: Because Iceberg retains historical snapshots and their underlying immutable data files, query engines can travel backward in time by referencing prior metadata states. Engines syntax like `TIMESTAMP AS OF` or `VERSION AS OF` instructs Iceberg to load the manifest list associated with the historical snapshot. This capability enables reproducible machine learning feature training, regulatory compliance auditing, and instantaneous rollback after faulty pipeline runs.
content.real_world_example: A financial bank ledger: if an erroneous automated billing script corrupted customer balances at midnight, engineers can query the table exactly as it existed at 23:59:59 to recalculate accurate transactions without restoring from tape backups.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Time travel relies on historical snapshots not being expired. If snapshot retention policies are set too aggressively (e.g. expiring after 24 hours), historical queries beyond that window will fail.
